title: Fig Bars
changes_from_base: A soft cookie base and lid around a fig and apple-juice filling, replacing caramel and chocolate.
summary: Soft brown sugar dough sandwiching a fig and apple-juice filling.
equipment: 20 cm square metal baking tin, lined with a baking-paper sling

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Simmer the figs, apple juice and pinch of salt 15-20 min, stirring now and then, until the figs are very soft and the liquid is syrupy. Cool a little, then blitz with the lemon juice to a thick jam.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Preheat to 175 °C (155 °C fan) with a sling-lined 20 cm tin ready. Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt. Beat the butter and sugar until pale, beat in the egg and vanilla, then mix in the flour. Set aside about a third (roughly 170 g).

steps.title: Base
steps.text: Press the rest evenly into the tin and bake about 20 min, until just turning golden. Meanwhile roll the reserved dough between greased sheets of baking paper into a 20 cm square and freeze it on a tray.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Spread the fig filling over the base, peel off the paper and lay the frozen square on top, pressing lightly.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 25-30 min, turning halfway, until golden. Cool 2 h in the tin, then cut into 16.

tips: Freezing the top layer makes it easy to place.
Choose soft dried figs and snip off the hard stems.
Cut with a sharp knife once completely cool.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 2 months.
